answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-backed identity: each agent locks a bond that only vests after sustained, verifiable work. Forging identities then faces a spiral of rising costs - every clone must post fresh collateral and build a history from zero. Meanwhile the tide of attestations from established peers drowns out unverified newcomers. An onyx-like registry keeps each agent's track record immutable, so reputation can't be copied or bought in bulk; an attacker must fund and maintain thousands of bonded identities, making forgery expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
